episodes.210925: A moderate upper level disturbance tapped into subtropical moisture resulting in thunderstorm activity across central and eastern NM, as well as virga showers and dry thunderstorms over western NM. A brief 59 mph virga induced gust hit the Four Corners Regional Airport in Farmington. A line of collapsing thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts in Union County, including a 66 mph gust at Clayton. Elsewhere, a brief tornado was observed by storm spotters near Corona, NM. Convective activity died down past sunset.
episodes.211296: An approaching shortwave interacted with ample moisture across west Texas, resulting in the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms. Cloud cover largely limited the severe threat, but one storm in the Big Bend did manage to produce severe wind gusts, up to 66 mph.
episodes.211795: A spring storm brought rain, mountain snow and thunderstorms to interior northern California in early to mid April. Gusty winds with a line of thunderstorms on April 11th between 5:00 PM and 9:00 PM led to numerous reports of tree damage and power outages in the Greater Sacramento Area and into the adjacent Sierra foothills, with measured wind gusts of 35 to 40 mph observed. There were also numerous reports of roadway flooding. A touchdown of an EF-U tornado occurred from 2:05 PM to 2:06 PM on April 12th near Vina, CA. There were also reports of severe hail in thunderstorms. Heavy mountain snow brought major travel impacts to the Sierra Nevada from April 10th through 12th. UC Berkeley Central Sierra Snow Lab measured 42.6 inches of heavy snow. Kirkwood Ski Resort measured 41 inches of heavy snow. Wind gusts in the Sierra were measured generally between 45 and 55 mph.
episodes.211867: Several rounds of heavy rainfall occurred across portions of north central Kansas on 4/10 and 4/11. This resulted in up to 11 inches of rainfall across portions of Marshall county by the early morning hours on 4/11. Roads were closed in the area and several people were stranded at a campground.  Later in the afternoon, additional severe storms caused large hail to around a half dollar size.
episodes.212480: A weakening line of thunderstorms moving northeast over East Central CO produced an outflow boundary that rushed east ahead of the storm activity into Kansas.  This boundary broke a healthy tree limb in Goodland.  As the weakening thunderstorms moved northeast into Kansas they produced wind gusts up to 76 MPH, the highest gust occurring at St. Francis.  Northwest of St. Francis these storms produced dust storm conditions.
episodes.212576: Thunderstorm outflow brought severe wind gusts to 3 counties.
episodes.212847: A broken line of weakening thunderstorms, originating from a sharpening dryline, moved northeast across east-central Colorado during the late afternoon and early evening hours. These weakening thunderstorms produced several severe wind gusts across east-central Colorado, including 73 mph recorded at Kit Carson County Airport. Severe winds also produced one-half mile visibility in blowing dust near Idalia.
episodes.212915: An isolated supercell thunderstorm developed across Kingman and Reno Counties during the afternoon hours of April 11. This storm produced winds up to 80 mph and up to golf ball size hail as it tracked across far northern Kingman, southern and eastern Reno, northern Sedgwick, and Harvey Counties.
episodes.213044: An isolated thunderstorm developed during the late afternoon hours of April 11th. This thunderstorm resulted in damaging winds across Reno County.
episodes.213102: A trough moved across Wyoming during the afternoon bringing high-based showers and thunderstorms. Dry air below storms lead to strong outflow wind gusts for much of central and western Wyoming. Wind gusts over 58 mph were reported in Fremont, Natrona, Johnson, Park, Lincoln and Sublette Counties. The highest wind gust reported was 83 mph at Red Canyon along Highway 28 through South Pass in Fremont County.
episodes.213204: A complex system brought severe winds to much of northern UT with a brief tornado along the border of Cache and Rich counties. Later on, this system would result in a flash flood event across southern UT.
episodes.213254: A complex system led to the development of thunderstorms across northern UT, eventually tracking into southwest WY resulting in multiple severe wind gusts along I-80.

The tornado is estimated to have touched down at 2:25PM MT approximately 1 mile south of the Sink Rd./HWY 89 intersection in far northwestern Rich county. The tornado promptly produced EF-1 damage snapping a few softwood trees. The tornado continued tracking north along the terrain into Cache county, increasing in width and producing a notably wider swath of softwood tree damage consistent with an EF-1 rating. The tornado then took a slight turn to the northeast and slightly weakened, producing a few more instances of EF-1 damage to softwood trees before dissipating in far southern Cache county at around 2:27PM. The maximum width of this tornado was 100 yards with a path length of 0.44 miles. Special thanks to the Cache and Rich county emergency managers for the assistance getting to the damage location, and another special thanks to our local spotters for reporting the damage.
